title: Planner: redesigned My Tasks experience on the web
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, automatic enablement and documented PowerShell control remain supported. The updated Planner admin guidance still includes My Tasks with qualifying Microsoft 365 licences; the broader entitlement wording should be qualified to match that guidance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Planner for admins says qualifying Microsoft 365 licences include task creation and editing capabilities.
claims.quote: Users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 license have access to a rich set of capabilities for individual and team work management. These capabilities include basic plan creation and editing capabilities, task creation and editing capabilities

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Planner for admins lists My Day and My Tasks among the capabilities available with a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence.
claims.quote: These capabilities include basic plan creation and editing capabilities, task creation and editing capabilities, various plan views - including Grid, Board, Schedule, and Charts - My Day, My Tasks, and more.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Planner app in Teams article says users with a Microsoft 365 licence are entitled to the Planner app.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 license are entitled to the Planner app.
claims.fix: Replace the unqualified entitlement sentence and corresponding licensing note with: 'Microsoft Learn lists My Day and My Tasks among the capabilities available with a qualifying Microsoft 365 licence that includes Planner.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/planner-for-admins, whose 20 November guidance names qualifying subscriptions rather than every Microsoft 365 licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model

claims.quote:
| Capability | Feature name | Microsoft Planner Included in Microsoft 365 | Planner Plan 1 | Planner and Project Plan 3 | Microsoft 365 Copilot |
|  | My Day and My Tasks | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is the documented PowerShell call for turning Planner off for the organisation.
claims.quote:
Turn off Planner for your organization using PowerShell

Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: An admin UI equivalent to the organisation-wide IsPlannerAllowed control, including its web reach, is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "IsPlannerAllowed" "admin center". Opened disable-planner, Planner for admins and manage-planner-app. The first documents PowerShell; the Teams admin UI blocks the Teams app, not the same organisation-wide web service control.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented organisation-wide PowerShell control requires a global admin.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Setting IsPlannerAllowed to $true turns Planner back on.
claims.quote:

Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $true
